errors.evidence: The time range on the x-axis extends to July 2025, not January 2025 as stated.
The purple line, representing the statutory minimum wage, remains steady at the initial value of 100 until January 2017, not July 2015.

errors.text_span: increases in steps to 102.2 in January 2016, 108.2 in January 2017, 111.8 in January 2018, 116.4 in January 2019, and 121.7 in January 2020, before rising more sharply to 122.7 in July 2020 and then to 145.7 in July 2022
errors.evidence: The sequence of dates and values described for the steps in the purple line is incorrect. For example, the first step up is in January 2017 to a value of approximately 103, not in Jan 2016 to 102.2. Subsequent dates and values are also wrong (e.g., the value in Jan 2019 is ~108, not 116.4). The listed values appear to be hallucinated.

errors.text_span: further increasing to 141.2 in October 2022 is not directly shown but is referenced in the legend
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly applies the legend information for the dark blue line to the purple line. The legend text "Index (Oktober 2022 = 141,2)" refers to the new index base for the dark blue line (contractual hourly wages), not a value reached by the purple line (statutory minimum wage).
The value of the light blue line in January 2021 is approximately 114, not 118.7. The value 118.7 is closer to the value in mid-2022.
The description of the light blue line ends at January 2021, but the line visibly continues on the chart until July 2022, reaching a value of approximately 120. This is a significant omission.
The description claims the dark blue line shows an increase starting in January 2022, but this line does not exist on the chart until later in 2022 (around July/October).
The value of the dark blue line in January 2025 is closer to 155. The stated value of 153.7 is slightly off and has unwarranted precision.
